help.monocarpic: Flowers only once and then dies, sometimes after many years (agave, bromeliad).
help.polycarpic: Flowers several times during its life (orchid, rose).
help.annual: Completes its whole life cycle in a single season.
help.biennial: Lives two years: leaves the first year, flowers the second.
help.perennial: Lives for several years. If it’s also monocarpic, it may flower only once after 10, 20 or 30 years, then die.

fingerTest.title: The finger test
fingerTest.body: Push a finger 2 to 3 cm into the soil: if it’s dry, it’s time to water.

roomTemperatureWater.title: No icy water
roomTemperatureWater.body: Water at room temperature so you don’t shock the roots.

drainage.title: Keep their feet dry
drainage.body: Empty the saucer 15 minutes after watering: standing water rots the roots.

dustyLeaves.title: Let the leaves breathe
dustyLeaves.body: A damp cloth on the leaves wipes off the dust that slows down photosynthesis.

quarterTurn.title: A quarter turn
quarterTurn.body: Turn your pots now and then so the plant doesn’t lean towards the window.

yellowLeaves.title: Yellow leaves?
yellowLeaves.body: It’s often too much water. Let the soil dry out before the next watering.

springRepotting.title: Repotting season
springRepotting.body: If roots are coming out of the pot, move to a slightly bigger one, 2 to 4 cm wider.

springFertilizer.title: Back to fertilizer
springFertilizer.body: Growth is picking up again: time to resume fertilizer, at the recommended dose or less.

summerWateringTime.title: Water when it’s cool
summerWateringTime.body: In summer, water early in the morning or in the evening: less water evaporates.

summerWindowBurn.title: Mind the window
summerWindowBurn.body: Behind a window in full sun, leaves can burn. A sheer curtain is enough to protect them.

autumnBringIn.title: Bring them in before the frost
autumnBringIn.body: Bring tender plants indoors before the first frosts, often as soon as nights drop to 10 °C.

autumnPests.title: Check before coming in
autumnPests.body: Before bringing a plant indoors, check under its leaves so you don’t invite pests in.

winterRadiators.title: Away from radiators
winterRadiators.body: The hot, dry air of a radiator dries out leaves. Move your plants away or group them together.

winterLessWater.title: Less water in winter
winterLessWater.body: Most plants are resting: water less often.

oldestTree.title: Over 4,800 years old!
oldestTree.body: Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine in California, is one of the oldest known trees.

bamboo.title: Almost a metre a day
bamboo.body: Some bamboos are among the fastest-growing plants in the world.

mimosa.title: A shy plant
mimosa.body: Mimosa pudica folds its leaves as soon as you touch them.

banana.title: A banana is a berry
banana.body: To botanists, a strawberry isn’t one!

monstera.title: Holes with a name
monstera.body: The holes in Monstera leaves are called fenestrations.

cactusSpines.title: Spines that used to be leaves
cactusSpines.body: In cacti, spines are leaves that changed shape to lose less water.

vanilla.title: Vanilla is an orchid
vanilla.body: Its pods are the fruit of a climbing orchid.

sunflower.title: Following the sun
sunflower.body: Young sunflowers follow the sun, then settle facing east once they bloom.
